entries.name: Great tit
behaviour: bold, confident begging-call in winter flocks of tits and nuthatches
inspects nest boxes by hovering at the hole, then inspects them all again next visit
very adaptable: parks, gardens and primary woodland alike

voxel_model.pattern: black head with white cheeks, yellow breast with black stripe

entries.notes: The benchmark songbird of the woodland garden feeder; black belly stripe is impossible to miss up close.

entries.name: Blue tit
behaviour: acrobatic upside-down feeder, hangs from twigs
necks down to the feeder hole; famously learned to steal doorstep milk in 1920s Britain
clutches up to 11+ eggs, among the largest of small birds

voxel_model.pattern: blue cap and wings, yellow belly, white face

entries.notes: The small, acrobatic corkscrew of the canopy; the largest brood size-to-body-mass ratio in the small songbirds.

entries.name: Eurasian nuthatch
behaviour: walks headfirst DOWN trunks, unique among tree-climbing birds
wedges nuts into bark cracks and hammers them open like a hatchet
plasters nest-hole entrances with mud to shrink the opening against invaders

voxel_model.pattern: slate-blue back, orange-rust belly, black eye-stripe

entries.notes: The upside-down tree walker; the mud-plugged nest hole is a dead giveaway of a tenanted tree.

entries.name: Common chaffinch
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern populations move south in autumn
behaviour: male sings a descending, shimmering rattle from a high perch
white wing-bars flash in flight
migrates in flocks that rain from the sky like seed

voxel_model.pattern: male: pink breast, blue-grey cap, white wing-bars

entries.notes: One of Europe's most common birds; a staple of the autumn finch flocks pouring out of the forest.

entries.name: Eurasian wren
behaviour: holds tail upright like a cocked revolver
explosively loud song for a bird the length of a thumb
male builds several 'cock nests' for females to choose from

voxel_model.pattern: barring on wings and tail, pale eyebrow stripe

entries.notes: A 10 g ball of aggression and song; you will hear it scolding you from the brambles before you see it.

entries.name: Song thrush
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern populations move south
behaviour: repeats each fluting phrase two to four times, unlike the blackbird's free-flowing song
smashes snails on a favoured stone, the 'thrush anvil'
leaves a carpet of broken shells under the anvil

voxel_model.pattern: spotted creamy breast, warm brown back

entries.notes: Find the pile of smashed snail shells on a flat stone; a song thrush's outdoor kitchen, permanently marked.

entries.name: Wood warbler
entries.migrates: long-distance migrant; winters in West Africa
behaviour: largest and purest-yellow of the leaf warblers
sunbird-like trill: a drawn-out crescendo 'velvety shimmer'
an indicator species of mature, unbroken broadleaf forest

voxel_model.pattern: lemon-yellow breast and eyebrow, olive back

entries.notes: Hear it before you see it, deep in high-forest canopies from late April to August; gone to Africa by September.

entries.name: Eurasian treecreeper
entries.migrates: mostly resident; partial migrant in the far north
behaviour: spirals UP a trunk like a tiny brown elf, then flies down and spirals the next tree
curved, tweezer-like bill extracts hidden beetle eggs from bark crevices
often joins mixed tit-nuthatch winter flocks

voxel_model.pattern: cryptic bark-marbled back, white belly

entries.notes: If the 'tiny brown thing' is climbing UP the trunk rather than down, it is this, not a nuthatch.

entries.name: Eurasian bullfinch
entries.migrates: partial migrant; many resident flocks wander
behaviour: glowing rose-red breast held very still, then a soft sad whistle
eats tree and fruit buds in spring; once culled as an 'orchard pest'
pairs stay together year-round

voxel_model.pattern: male rose-red breast, black cap and wings, white rump

entries.notes: The blushing ghost of cold-season woodland; nearly silent but unmistakable in silhouette and breast colour.

entries.name: Eurasian blackcap
entries.migrates: long-distance migrant; winters in North Africa and southern Europe
behaviour: rich, rambling song that even birdwatchers call the 'northern nightingale'
male with a neat black cap, female rusty-brown
growing British winter population: now a common garden bird

voxel_model.pattern: male: black cap on grey back; female: rufous cap

entries.notes: A large-headed warbler with theatre-worthy singing; its winter quarters have shifted north into gardens.

entries.name: Eurasian pygmy owl
entries.migrates: resident; partial nomadic movements in lean years
behaviour: hunts small songbirds in broad daylight from a hidden branch
nests in old woodpecker holes
caches surplus kills speared onto branches
sounds: steady, high PEEP-PEEP-PEEP recalling a cricket

voxel_model.pattern: brown back with white spots, false 'eyes' on the nape

entries.notes: Europe's smallest owl; its nape 'false eyes' may confuse predators striking from behind. Cached victims speared on branches are its signature.

entries.name: Eurasian sparrowhawk
behaviour: extreme sexual dimorphism: the female is nearly twice the male's mass
bursts of explosive speed between trunks to ambush garden songbirds
chased to near-extinction by DDT; now back in city gardens

voxel_model.pattern: grey (male) or brown (female) back, red-barred chest, long tail

entries.notes: The stealth hawk of the suburban canopy; nests built in dense woodland conifers, its recovery tracks the return of woodland cover.

entries.name: European nightjar
entries.migrates: long-distance migrant; winters in sub-Saharan Africa
behaviour: sits on the ground by day, utterly invisible among dead bracken
'churrs' like a strimmer at dusk; males clap wings over the back in display
eats on the wing, boomerang-like through the clearing edge

voxel_model.pattern: mottled cryptic browns, white throat and wing spots

entries.notes: The ghost of the summer ride: a huge-eyed, moth-hawking bird you locate only by its unending dusk rattle.

entries.name: Field vole
behaviour: grass-edge specialist of woodland rides and tussocky verges
runs along vole 'motorways' of clipped grass tunnels
cycles: boom years then predator-driven crashes

voxel_model.pattern: blunt muzzle, dark flanks fading to grey

entries.notes: The engine room of the woodland food web; when voles crash, owls, stoats and kestrels feel it within weeks.

entries.name: Common shrew
behaviour: highest metabolic rate of any land mammal; must eat every 2-3 hours or it starves
'caravan' behaviour: mother leads a train of clinging young tail-to-tail
half of its body behind the head; heart rate near 800 beats per minute

voxel_model.pattern: dark back, russet flanks, pale belly

entries.notes: The twitching bullet of the leaf litter; voracious for its size and fabulously territorial for a 8 g animal.

entries.name: Eurasian pygmy shrew
behaviour: second-lightest mammal in Europe after the white-toothed shrews
favours damper, mossy forest-floor microhabitats
vanishes instantly under bark when disturbed

voxel_model.pattern: more uniform brown than the common shrew, greyer belly

entries.notes: The kingdom's lightest shrew; you will never see one and never stop flipping logs in the hope.

entries.name: Yellow-necked mouse
behaviour: strong leaper, bounds through the lower canopy like a mini red squirrel
builds round leaf nests in hollows and old birdboxes
shiny, bright-eyed, trotting the forest floor on warm nights

voxel_model.pattern: orange collar fading to white belly, white feet

entries.notes: The big, golden-collared cousin of the wood mouse; a strong climber that owns the oak canopy at night.

entries.name: Eurasian harvest mouse
behaviour: Britain's smallest rodent; hangs from grass stems by its prehensile tail
weaves spherical grass nests high among standing stems
surveyed by searching for the summer nests after harvest

voxel_model.pattern: golden-russet above, paper-white below

entries.notes: Woodland-edge and hedgerow specialist; find its hanging woven ball and you have found the only British mammal nesting above ground in standing grass.

entries.name: Garden dormouse
behaviour: hibernates up to seven months in a leaf-lined tree hollow from October
the most carnivorous dormouse: preys on the nests of other small animals
black 'bandit' mask from nose to ear distinguishes it from all other dormice

voxel_model.pattern: black mask, black-and-white tipped bushy tail

entries.notes: Europe's fastest-declining mammal (IUCN 2024: Vulnerable); hibernation and insect decline have emptied its range east of the Rhine.

entries.name: Edible dormouse (fat dormouse)
behaviour: famously plump before winter; Romans fattened dormice in gliraria for the table
hibernates October to May in cork-dry tree hollows, sometimes together in huddles
breeds in bumper beech and oak mast years; silent in barren years

voxel_model.pattern: ash-grey back, white belly, dark-ringed big eyes

entries.notes: Giacomo Puccini and Roman feasts notwithstanding, do not confuse a fat grey shape in your attic with a squirrel: far fluffier tail, no bark-stripping.

entries.name: Northern flying squirrel
behaviour: glides between trunks up to 65 m on a furry patagium stretched ankle to wrist
communal nesting: families huddle in tree cavities for winter warmth
single most important disperser of mycorrhizal truffles in northern forests

voxel_model.pattern: cinnamon-grey above, flat paddle tail, huge dark eyes

entries.notes: The truffle-ferried ghost of the northern canopy; a reddish eye-shine in torchlight is the way to spot it.

entries.name: Stoat (ermine)

breeding.season: summer mating, births next spring (delayed implantation)

behaviour: turns pure white in winter above the snow line: the 'ermine'
famously kills far more than it can eat, taking rabbits larger than itself
black tuft at the very tip of the tail, all year

voxel_model.pattern: white belly, black tail tip; full white ermine phase in snow country

entries.notes: The violent ribbon of the vole tunnels; mating happens in summer, implantation is delayed, and kits arrive the following spring.

entries.name: European polecat
behaviour: wild ancestor of the ferret; hybridises with feral ferrets
anal glands blast a horrific musky stink when threatened
favours damp lowlands, water meadows and woodland edges

voxel_model.pattern: dark guard hairs over yellow underfur, pale eye-mask

entries.notes: Smell it before you see it; once persecuted to near-extinction in Britain, now re-spreading west across the Midlands.

entries.name: Beech marten (stone marten)

breeding.season: summer mating, births in spring (delayed implantation)

behaviour: white throat bib like a cravat; the town-marten, happy in roofs and car engine bays
notorious for chewing wiring and coolant hoses
leaps like a cat and climbs like a squirrel

voxel_model.pattern: brown coat with the white throat bib

entries.notes: If an animal is screaming on your roof at 2 a.m. and is bigger than a cat, this is your prime suspect.

entries.name: European mole
behaviour: eats its body weight in worms daily; has a dedicated worm 'larder' chamber with bitten heads so they stay fresh
swims through loose soil by breast-stroke burrowing
moles underline woodland rides and grassy clearings with ridges

voxel_model.pattern: velvety charcoal, pink bare paddle hands

entries.notes: Almost never seen above ground; the fresh molehill is the only signature of one of the busiest carnivores underground.

entries.name: Common lizard (viviparous lizard)

breeding.season: spring rut; live birth in late summer

behaviour: the only truly live-bearing lizard of northern Europe; births young in a thin membrane it tears immediately
basks on stumps at 25-30 degrees; retreats underground at the first shiver
can shed and regrow its tail

voxel_model.pattern: mottled brown or olive, dorsal stripe on males; gold flanks in breeding season

entries.notes: The basker of sunny stumps in woodland rides; live birth lets it breed far north of any egg-laying lizard's range.

entries.name: Slow worm

breeding.season: spring mating; live birth in late summer

behaviour: a legless LIZARD, not a snake: it blinks, has eyelids and a notched tongue
communal hibernacula of dozens under log piles and compost heaps
autotomises its tail readily; the shed end writhes to distract predators

voxel_model.pattern: males: golden body with dark flanks and blue tail speckles

entries.notes: The garden-log turned end; excellent biological control of slugs, and fond of the compost corner.

entries.name: Common toad
entries.migrates: mass spring migration to the natal breeding pond
behaviour: warty skin and parotoid glands ooze bufotoxin: unpalatable to most predators
crawls stiff-legged and plodding, unlike the frog's spring
females return to the exact pond of their own tadpolehood
sounds: thin croak-buzz from the pond chorus

voxel_model.pattern: warty olive-brown, golden iris

entries.notes: Toad-in-the-hole of the spring migration; thousands of patient commuters crossing roads after the first warm, wet nights.

entries.name: Smooth newt (common newt)

breeding.season: spring; eggs folded individually into pond leaves

behaviour: males grow a wavy crest and orange flanks in the breeding season
displays in shallows: tail fanning to waft pheromones at the female
spends most of the year on land in damp vegetation

voxel_model.pattern: male breeding: spotted orange flanks, dark back

entries.notes: The pond-courtship fan-dancer you can find under a paving slab on a rainy June night.

entries.name: Great crested newt
behaviour: breeding male grows a jagged dinosaur crest from neck to tail tip
largest British newt; bright orange belly with bold black blotches
legally protected across Europe: handling one is a matter for the licence holder

voxel_model.pattern: black-marbled back, orange warty flanks, white tail flash in courtship

entries.notes: The dragon of the garden pond; strictly protected in Europe and a licensing headache for any developer who drains a woodland pond.

entries.name: Southern wood ant

breeding.season: spring; queens mate in nuptial flights

behaviour: builds towering thatch domes of twigs and pine needles to warm the brood
tends and herds aphid herds up and down the trees, milking honeydew
sprays formic acid; protected across Europe and reintroduced to Britain

voxel_model.pattern: dark red head and thorax, black-tipped abdomen

entries.notes: The single most important ant of European woodland; its mounds are protected monuments to cooperative insect engineering.

entries.name: Purple emperor

breeding.season: midsummer; caterpillars overwinter half-grown on sallow twigs

behaviour: spends its life high in mature oaks; nearly invisible except when it drops to feed
males converge on high 'master trees' and duel with spiraling aerial combat
caterpillars eat only sallow (goat willow and relatives)

voxel_model.pattern: male: blackish wings with a violet sheen, white bands and orange-ringed eyespots

entries.notes: The holy grail of British butterflying; one oak per master-tree on the wood's highest point is all a colony asks.

entries.name: European peacock butterfly

breeding.season: spring (adults emerge and mate in summer, after diapause)

behaviour: angular, scalloped wings with huge iridescent eyespots to startle predators
larvae feed in conspicuous black, spiny communal clusters on nettles
overwinters as an adult in hollow trees and sheds and wakes on the first warm days
sounds: a click of wings when a predator lunges

voxel_model.pattern: russet ground with huge blue-spotted eyespots on each wing

entries.notes: The four-eyed nettle-eater; the loudest snap of open wings in the woodland courtship show.

entries.name: European rhinoceros beetle

breeding.season: summer; larvae develop 3-5 years in dead wood

behaviour: male's magnificent curved horn is a weapon for rival fights and digging tunnels
grub can reach 11 cm, dwarfing the eventual 3.5 cm beetle
adults do not feed at all; they fly to lights on June and July evenings

voxel_model.pattern: glossy mahogany, male with long upturned horn

entries.notes: Protected in Germany and a flagship of dead-wood habitat; its sawdust-grub years outnumber its two months of summer horn-sport.

entries.name: Common shiny woodlouse
behaviour: a land-going CRUSTACEAN; still aquatic-grade: breathes through gill-like pleopods and needs humidity
mother carries the pale 'mancae' in a fluid pouch (marsupium) beneath her body
curls tight when flicked; prefers the underside of water-logged logs

voxel_model.pattern: polished slate-brown, pale side spots

entries.notes: The forest's cleanup crew, armoured like a tiny tank; compost heaps and log piles without woodlice process leaf litter far more slowly.

entries.name: Common earthworm
behaviour: engineers the soil: one worm turns its own depth in soil casts per year
drags whole leaves into its burrow by anchoring its tail and pulling
surface casts at dawn betray the midnight gardener's route

voxel_model.pattern: pink-brown cylinder, darker head, red saddle (clitellum)

entries.notes: The best fisherman's friend and the forest's quiet frontpage; without it the floor of your world simply stops working.

entries.name: Great black slug
behaviour: Europe's largest land slug; jet black, sometimes dusty grey-orange
contracts into a glistening, eyeless knob when disturbed
feeds as much on dead things as leaves; the forest's undertaker

voxel_model.pattern: uniform gunmetal black, sometimes dark grey or orange-brown form

entries.notes: The size of your thumb and the colour of old tar; the rainy-night archaeologist that keeps the dead out of the soil's books.
